analysis: All supplied units are documentation or changelog text only: changelog.d/landing-agent-discovery.md, docs/README.md, docs/architecture/README.md, docs/architecture/components/landing.md (new), and docs/developer/build.md. There are no code changes in this batch, so no authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or provider-routing behavior changes here. The docs describe a landing/ site that gains Markdown negotiation, a public sitemap, an OpenAPI description, and server-side pricing fetch. The landing.md claims need verification against the actual landing/ source, which is not in this batch: pricing.ts must fetch a fixed public upstream and not forward visitor credentials (landing.md:38, so no SSRF); proxy.ts must derive canonical identity from config, not the Host header (landing.md:34, relevant to T-040); and the static openapi.json must not imply new auth paths. The docs/architecture/README.md change removes the 'landing/ site' mention from the console-ui row and adds a landing row; this is a doc relocation only. build.md describes applying a version-pinned patch to Next.js build artifacts. This is a build-supply-chain concern that is out of scope for the threat model (GitHub Actions/R2 supply chain). No threat-model assumptions are invalidated by this batch. The next pass should inspect the landing/ source files (proxy.ts, pricing.ts, public-site.ts, openapi.json, the Next patch script) if they are included in other batches. Missing source is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
